timeline.title: The HUD, and the shape of the thing
timeline.detail: 19 screens, five tabs, the reactor. One reducer for the link so every tab agrees about what is connected.

timeline.title: Named places and located answers
timeline.detail: Coordinates resolved on the phone, because `KnownPlace` exists nowhere else. Unverified since the fix that touched it.

timeline.title: The journal, and derived facts only
timeline.detail: Usage read on the device, rolled up, and shared as a rollup rather than rows. The pattern every later sense copies — and the reason a notification listener is designable at all.

timeline.title: Every state must name itself
timeline.detail: It came up five times in one day. The briefing that never ran and the briefing that ran and found nothing to say were indistinguishable from outside, which let a wrong hypothesis stand for a day.

timeline.title: Background work: measured, not assumed
timeline.detail: `expo-background-task` hardcodes `setRequiredNetworkType(CONNECTED)`, and the uid reads `blocked=REASON_APP_BACKGROUND|REASON_APP_STANDBY` with `#netAvail=0` in a RARE bucket. **Stopped, not deferred.** Every presence decision since is chosen around this.

timeline.title: He speaks first — and gets it wrong
timeline.detail: The first unprompted remark asserted a Saturday shift on a Friday. A bare substring test matched a Mon–Fri work pattern, and the prompt then asserted it as true today. Fixed in the brain the same day; still undeployed.

timeline.title: The briefing arrives twice
timeline.detail: Naming Home armed both senders at once — the gateway push and the phone's own task, byte-identical strings so the shade could not tell them apart. The old plan said *keep the local task as a fallback*; it was never gated, so it was a second sender.

timeline.title: A local build silently breaks OTA
timeline.detail: `prebuild` writes the literal `file:fingerprint` into `strings.xml`; EAS substitutes the real hash and a local Gradle build does not. The APK then asks for updates matching a placeholder, gets none, and runs its embedded bundle forever. Nothing logs a word. Cost an hour.

timeline.title: The status panel, and anticipation v1
timeline.detail: Eight seams, four states, assembled on the device so it reads with nothing connected — which is exactly when it is looked at. Anticipation decides in code from the journal against its own baseline.

timeline.title: The OTA channel gate closed
timeline.detail: One command, read-only. Channel Active, branch linked, runtime byte-identical to the installed APK. The fear was an empty channel — the app asks and gets nothing, silently. It is not empty.

timeline.title: One source of truth for status
timeline.detail: Three files were carrying status claims and drifting. Now `docs/status/ledger.json` holds them all and everything else is generated, so a percentage cannot disagree with the row it came from.

timeline.title: The briefing row stops asserting what it cannot know
timeline.detail: A workspace-only week ages the upload stamp, and the panel read that as the gateway having lost the schedule. Three states now. The task's gate is untouched — a stale stamp still means the phone posts.

timeline.title: An npm script changes the runtime fingerprint
timeline.detail: `packageJson:scripts` is a fingerprint input. Adding two convenience scripts moved the runtime from `31c64113` to `3f9be979`, and the first OTA publish went to a runtime **no device has** — arriving nowhere, with a success message. Caught by reading the publish output against the installed fingerprint. The scripts were removed; the generator is invoked directly.

queue.title: Confirm the OTA channel
queue.detail: Was one command and gated every JS-only fix behind it. Channel `production` Active, branch linked, runtime byte-identical to the installed APK. **Proved end to end:** the publish that followed landed on the matching runtime, which is the only thing this check ever claimed.

queue.title: The briefing-schedule row stops lying
queue.detail: A workspace-only week ages the upload stamp, and the panel asserted the gateway lost the schedule — which the phone cannot know. Three states now: `AT THE GATEWAY`, `CANNOT TELL`, `ON THIS PHONE`. `cloudArmedState()` sits beside `cloudArmed()`, so the task gate is untouched and a stale stamp still means the phone posts. 10 tests; committed `d5eff11`; published to runtime `31c64113`. **On the phone 2026-08-24:** the new bundle is live (the update server serves it for this exact runtime and the app reports nothing newer), the panel renders, and the briefing row reads `AT THE GATEWAY` correctly while the link is cloud. **Still owed:** the new `CANNOT TELL` state itself is unreachable on a cloud-linked phone — the stamp is fresh — so it needs two days of workspace-only sessions or a debug build.

queue.title: The chat log in the right order, once each
queue.detail: **The ordering half is fixed; the duplicate half already was.** The note this item carried was stale — it asked for the real `at` values before more code, and `96de0e1` had already got them from a shipped audit and turned the exact-millisecond key into a 5-second window. What remained was that the chat rendered in ARRIVAL order: `ChatScreen` reversed the array without ever sorting by `at`, so a turn swept out of the tray carrying last night's stamp was appended last and read as the newest — yesterday's `15:xx` below today's `12:xx`, the second reported symptom. Fixed in the reducer rather than at the reader, because two readers assumed the array was ordered and `activity.ts` sorted the same data before showing it. 4 tests, 2 failed first; 999 tests green, `tsc` clean. **Closed 2026-08-27 on the phone**, on `01a0429e`, by scrolling the whole log rather than reading one screen — the previous fix here was called done from a screenshot and was not.

queue.title: Provider effects that outlive their tree
queue.detail: **Closed 2026-08-26.** An effect resolving after its test body corrupts the act environment, after which every later render returns an empty tree — no throw, no warning. It cost six tests. Fixed where `jarvisProvider.test.tsx` said it had to be: at the source, not inside each `.then`. `state/live.ts` is a per-run cancellation scope — a factory rather than a hook, because a provider-lifetime guard cannot cancel a dependency change and the alert registration at `[alert?.id, alert]` needs exactly that. All nine settle sites open one and end it from the effect cleanup; the one that hands a registration back on a dead run keeps its `l.alive` branch, named explicitly in a test so a second exception cannot appear quietly. The inventory is the argument for a primitive: eight sites carried a hand-written `let alive` and the ninth did not, and nothing could have told you which. 13 tests — 8 on the scope, 5 on the provider, including a source scan that fails if a bare settle reappears. Proved by mutation: reinstating the bare `.then` fails the scan, restoring it passes. No device needed, and none used.

queue.title: A crash says what it was
queue.detail: **The JS half is written and green as of 2026-08-28. Nothing has been published, and nothing has been seen on the phone.** A crash used to restart in silence, with `adb logcat` on the one machine that built the APK as the only diagnosis. Now: a derived record — no chat text, no token, because a crash log is exactly what gets pasted into a chat window — written by the boundary for a render crash and by a wrapped global handler for everything else, read back at Settings → Diagnostics with a count on the row for what has not been looked at. **What is left is a publish and a look at the phone.** A native crash still needs a service and a build, and stays owed rather than quietly folded in.

queue.title: He answers out loud
queue.detail: Voice out is the largest single gap in the chat, and app-only. The decision of whether and what to speak is pure and testable; the native call sits at the edge. Stop any utterance in flight before starting the next — two voices over each other is worse than none.

queue.title: He comes back after a reboot
queue.detail: **Closed 2026-08-27 on the device, and it cost no code at all.** The phone was rebooted on the night of 26 Aug with the run count on Places at **22**, and the app was not opened afterwards. A briefing arrived at 07:00, and the count read **28** when the app was first opened that morning — six runs nobody started, from a process that had been killed by a reboot. WorkManager rescheduled its own queue at boot, which is exactly the bar `TESTING.md` 1.9 sets. By 10:27 it read 37. The premise this item was written on had already been corrected on 2026-08-26: `dumpsys package` on the installed APK says `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED: granted=true`, `expo-task-manager` declares a receiver on `BOOT_COMPLETED`, and there was never anything to build here — only a check nobody had run. **The 07:00 run cannot be read after the fact:** the heartbeat keeps one outcome, not a history, so nine later runs have overwritten whatever that one recorded.

queue.title: Speak into the microphone
queue.detail: **Run on 2026-08-27 and no longer the oldest unverified thing here.** Held the mic, said *"hi jarvis"*, and `brains.usage.audio` moved from all zeros to `gemini_ok: 1` with no fallback and no error — so the audio reaches the gateway and Gemini accepts the m4a. The mime worry was unfounded: `_AUDIO_MIME` already maps `m4a` to `audio/aac`. **What is left is accuracy, not plumbing:** the transcript read *"ki service"*, and the reply was correct Benglish for that question rather than for the one asked. `_GEMINI_TRANSCRIBE_PROMPT` primes for romanised Bengali by design and overcorrects on plain English — a gateway change, so it waits with the rest of the brain work.

queue.title: The journal denial path, and the other never-run paths
queue.detail:
Settings → Journal → usage access off → return. It must say *I cannot see your usage*, never *Nothing recorded*. Built, tested, and never once run by a human. Same sitting: the location timeline and anticipation v1, both unexercised for the same reason.

**RUN 2026-09-03, and it passes on both halves.** Usage access revoked from the laptop (`appops set … android:get_usage_stats deny`), the app restarted, and the Journal read:

> **NO ACCESS** · TODAY — *"I cannot see your usage, sir — the permission is off."* · HELD ON THIS DEVICE — Moments **52,598**, Day totals 921, Leaves the phone **Never**

**It says *cannot see*, never *nothing recorded* — and it proves the difference by still showing the 52,598 moments it holds.** A screen claiming an empty journal over three years of stored moments is the failure this row was written to catch.

**And it healed.** Permission restored, app restarted: *ON THIS PHONE* · *"5h 23m on the phone, sir, across 43 pickups. Facebook 56m, Instagram 50m, eFootball 45m"* · *"Last synced 1:08 PM. 47 new moments"* — it caught up what it could not see while it was denied.

The two siblings named in this entry are closed as well: `timeline` was proved on 08-27 and `anticipate-v1` on 09-02.

queue.title: Usable by someone who cannot see it well
queue.detail: Better than the old ledger admitted: contrast is measured at 4.78 and 4.68 against a 4.5 bar, and reduced motion already follows the OS with a test on it. What is genuinely owed is the label audit and a TalkBack pass.

queue.title: The photo half of the chat
queue.detail: **Two of the three parts were already built, which the queue did not know.** The thumbnail renders and a photo turn already marks itself `SENDING` / `NOT SENT`. What was genuinely missing, and is now built (2026-08-31), is recovery: a failed photo could not be re-sent, because the bytes went to the socket and only a local uri stayed in the log. It now re-encodes from that uri, keeps the caption, and says so plainly when the cached file is gone. Unpublished and unproved on the phone.

queue.title: Appearance surviving a launch
queue.detail: **Built 2026-08-31.** Accent, glow and motion survive a launch, with motion stored tri-state so an untouched switch keeps following the OS. Cheap, ships over the air, and immediately visible — which is exactly why it mattered that the row claimed it for days while it was in-memory.

queue.title: The notification listener
queue.detail: The step change in presence — event-driven, nearly free, and more context than any polling can buy. **Gated on the token split, which is gateway work:** a listener sees OTPs, balances and private messages, and once that is collected badly no later fix un-collects it. What can be built now is the spec and the pure drop-rule reducer, with no service registered and no permission asked.

queue.title: Split APP_TOKEN by capability
queue.detail: One string gates the socket, push, `/app-commute` and `/app-state` alike, and nothing expires. The gateway validates both halves, so it cannot land here. The gate in front of every new sense, not a follow-up.

queue.title: Merge fix/durable-state, then deploy
queue.detail: **Done, 2026-08-29.** `c86d176` is contained in `origin/feat/cloud-gateway`, so the briefing is no longer disarmed by a deploy and the false Saturday shift is live. Verified from this repo by `git branch -r --contains`, which is as much as this laptop can check.

queue.title: The situation sent to the persona
queue.detail: Place, battery, link — one field on the envelope. The most character per line of code available anywhere in the plan, and it is a gateway change.

queue.title: Delivered and read ticks
queue.detail: The phone knows *sent*. Only the gateway can say *delivered* and *read*, and it says neither. Needs a per-message id on both sides — and reply-to-a-message wants the same id, so it follows rather than inventing a second identity for a message.

queue.title: The desk-key handshake, and rotate BRIDGE_SECRET
queue.detail: 18 sealed turns dropped and rising, so the encrypted path has never once worked end to end. The old secret went through a log and still opens `/desk-link`. **The only item whose cost grows while deferred** — do both in one sitting rather than waiting for the desk twice.

queue.title: Run run_harnesses.py
queue.detail: Never executed by a Python interpreter with the real imports. This laptop has no Python — `python` opens the Microsoft Store. A duplicated-call SyntaxError already slipped through once and was caught by reading.

queue.title: A real release keystore
queue.detail: Release is signed with Expo's generated debug keystore, which is why a local APK and an EAS-signed one cannot replace each other. Fine for one phone, and the blocker on the second. **Folded into queue 23 on 2026-08-27** — it is free during a build that is happening anyway, and the spec sequences it with the other three.

queue.title: The Iron Man styling pass
queue.detail: Scope is styling: the logo does not change and no copy changes. The pieces exist and are under-used. Land it on one screen and live with it for a day before propagating — the item most likely to sprawl. The Android glass blur stays last of all: it adds no capability and its failure mode is a segfault that takes the process.

queue.title: Promote what he is told into what he knows
queue.detail:
Today he learns four things, all about the phone: screen time, pickups, top apps, plus named places. He learns **nothing** from what you say — the only route from a sentence to a durable fact is typing it into the Memory screen yourself. Meanwhile the chat window holds about a day and rolls silently. The pattern to copy already exists and is proved: `shareFacts` derives, keeps a ledger of what it already sent, supersedes what changed, and — critically — sends **derived facts, never raw rows**. A turn-to-fact pass wants the same shape and the same restraint, plus a rule about consent, because quietly distilling everything a person says is a different product from one that remembers what it was told.

**2026-09-02: built and proved, and it turned up the thing the queue item did not know.** Candidates on the Memory screen, kept or dismissed by hand, sending nothing until ticked; plus the mirror pass that offers stale facts up for forgetting. Proved on the phone the same evening: 18 KNOWN to 19 on a keep, then 18 to 15 on three forgets.

**The gateway was already distilling chat into facts by itself** — it wrote its own paraphrase the instant the sentence was sent. That is the quiet option this design explicitly refused, running server-side the whole time. The phone now has the consent-based half and a way to tidy up after the other one; **switching the silent half off is one change on the gateway** and is the thing to do first when brain work resumes.

queue.title: A day boundary in the chat
queue.detail: **Already built, found 2026-08-31 by reading the screen rather than the row.** `DayRule` renders a rule with the day's name between one day's turns and the next (`ChatScreen.tsx`), placed on the oldest turn of each day, with `dayHeading` pinned by its own tests. Nothing was written for this today except this correction.

queue.title: The gateway briefing repeats itself too
queue.detail: **WRITTEN on the home machine 2026-08-29 (`02604c6`) and NOT LIVE.** Ported from this repo's `src/lib/briefingVoice.ts` line for line rather than reinvented, because two senders with two voices is worse than the repetition: a pool per slot, one cursor object shared across departures, the figures never varied, and the actionable word (`umbrella`, `jacket`, `Water`, `hair`, `wait it out`) kept in every variant, since Android truncates a body in the shade. The cursor is spent only on a briefing that actually went out — `_push_all` returns whether anything left, and a push that reached nobody now leaves the day OPEN rather than marking it done, which is the rule the failed-forecast path already had. It persists through `_persist("briefing_voice")` and is restored on boot, the half that waited on durable state: a cursor a deploy resets restarts the rotation at the same line every time. `_briefing_text` without a cursor still draws the first line of every pool, so the prose the harness asserts is unchanged; `test_commute_briefing.py` 15 -> 26, negative-tested by committing the cursor before the push instead of after. **Owed: a deploy, then two mornings of looking at the notification.**

queue.title: The next native build — alarms, battery, background sightings, keystore
queue.detail:
**Specced 2026-08-27, awaiting approval: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-next-native-build-design.md`.** Prompted by *"can the app set alarms?"* — it cannot, and it says so honestly in the log. `AlarmClock.ACTION_SET_ALARM` would be perhaps forty lines, **and it cannot be published**: `android.permissions` is a fingerprint input, so one permission moves the runtime and a publish then reaches no device at all.

So the unit of work is the APK, not the feature, and **three other things have been waiting for one**: `expo-battery` for the missing half of §3.2.1, `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` for the `timeline` row's structural weakness (sightings only happen when the app is opened), and the real release keystore from queue 18, which is free during a build that is happening anyway. Spending a build on alarms alone and finding the next item a week later is the failure the spec exists to prevent.

**Background location is the one to argue separately** — it is the only item that changes what the app knows while closed. The alarm design is deliberately narrow: recognised on the phone rather than by the model (`asOpenAppCommand`'s rule, since a model asked to set an alarm can only say it did), ambiguity declines — *"set an alarm for 6:30"* is twice a day and asks — and `EXTRA_SKIP_UI` stays false so a human confirms what a regex parsed.

**2026-09-01: the background-sightings half shipped, and the build was local.** `expo-location` with `isAndroidBackgroundLocationEnabled`, `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`, and a WATCH control on Places. The OTA runtime moved `31c64113` to `1818e1b7`, which is why the code and the manifest were deliberately split across two sittings: the geofence library landed first and shipped over the air, and only the manifest change waited for a build.

**Queue 18 was NOT taken in the same build, and the reason is data.** The installed app is signed with `android/app/debug.keystore` (cert `fac61745dc09`), so a build signed with any other key — EAS included — cannot update it. The only way to install one is to uninstall first, and that costs the journal, the chat archive and the sightings. **Corrected 2026-09-03: the sightings are twelve DAYS, not twelve weeks** — the phone reports 138 rows reaching back 12 days. Twelve weeks was the old store's TTL, mistaken for its contents. A real keystore now means either accepting that loss or doing signing-scheme v3 key rotation, which is a separate job. `adb install -r` with the same key keeps everything, and that is what was done.

Still owed by this queue item: the alarm intent, and `expo-battery` for §3.2.1.

queue.detail: **FIXED on the home machine 2026-08-29, `efd1af1`, and unproved from the phone.** Both halves landed together as the handoff asked: the destination is preferred from a `to` phrasing and `here` / `my location` / `current location` are rejected, and the stale `currently` fact is no longer stored as permanent. **What is owed now is one question asked out loud from somewhere that is not home** — *"how far is home from here"* — which is the phrasing that was never tried and the whole reason this survived so long. **Closed 2026-09-01**: asked from the Office in the exact phrasing, answered with measured road distance and time.

queue.title: A spoken turn that outlives its socket arrives with no question above it
queue.detail: **BOTH HALVES ARE WRITTEN, on the home machine, 2026-08-29 — and neither is live.** Gateway `2301ad7` on `feat/cloud-gateway`: the transcript `emit()` result is read rather than discarded, and when the socket died before it left, the text rides on the reply's push as `data.transcript`. App half in this repo: `replyFromData` reads that field for `kind: reply` only, `take()` dispatches a `transcript` frame above the answer with the same `at`, and the reducer deduplicates a user turn the way it already did a pushed reply — the tray sweep re-enters the same notification on every return to the foreground, which would otherwise have appended his question again under its own answer. **What is owed is a deploy and a publish, not code:** Render has to take the gateway commit and the app half has to go out over the air before anyone can see it. Then the device proof, which is the original repro — ask by voice, pocket the phone, and read what the chat shows when it comes back. Tests: `test_app_link.py` 42 -> 46 (three drive the real handler with `send_json` failing on exactly the frame a pocketed phone loses; one pins the discarded-`emit` statement form a refactor would restore), and 1119 jest across 80 suites here, typecheck clean. **2026-08-31: both halves are committed and neither is on the phone.** The gateway half is live; the app half is `6d8be2d` here, waiting with everything else on an OTA publish. Until that publish, a spoken turn that outlives its socket still arrives as an answer with no question above it — which looks exactly like the original defect and is not it.

queue.title: Secure everything the phone now holds
queue.detail:
**Asked for on 2026-09-03, and asked to be kept last on purpose** — after the features, before anyone else ever touches this phone.

**What changed is what is held.** A month ago this app carried a chat log and a pairing token. It now holds twelve weeks of named-place sightings with times, every geofence crossing, a journal of 52,000 usage moments, a growing chat archive, memory facts about family and work — and, once the next build lands, the call log. **That is a life, on one device, in plain SQLite and AsyncStorage.**

The pass wants a threat model first and a list of fixes second, because "secure the app" without naming what from is how security work becomes theatre. The obvious candidates, roughly in order of what they buy:

1. **At rest.** AsyncStorage and the SQLite files are readable by anything with the device unlocked and adb, and by a full backup. `android:allowBackup` and the data-extraction rules decide whether a life leaves on a cable.
2. **The token.** Already in SecureStore; check nothing else sensitive sits beside it in AsyncStorage.
3. **On screen.** `FLAG_SECURE` keeps the chat, the memory and the map out of the recents thumbnail and out of screenshots taken by other apps.
4. **In logs.** The crash record already redacts on the digits-not-length rule; the same discipline has to cover anything new that logs a place, a number or a name.
5. **Off the phone.** What the gateway receives is already derived rather than raw, and the call-log design keeps that: an alias and a boolean, never a number. That rule needs holding as the surfaces grow.

**App lock and biometrics already exist and are not this.** They stop somebody opening the app; they do nothing about a cable, a backup, or a screenshot.

queue.title: Import seventeen months of Google Timeline
queue.detail:
**The plan is written and Task 1 of five is done.** Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-archive-import.md`, 1,614 lines, every step carrying its code. Plan A shipped and is proved on the phone (138 rows, 12 days), so the table that can hold the export exists.

**Tasks 1 and 2 — done and PUBLISHED 2026-09-04 as `ac6cf0a5`, runtime unmoved at `5f318efe`.** Task 1 (`6adf351`): `Seen.via` gains `import-enter` and `import-exit`; `leftBy` and `arrivalHour` count imported rows and return a `source`; `putMany`, `dropImported` and `forgetImported` exist. 1,495 tests, 102 suites, runtime unmoved at `5f318efe`.

Task 2 (`25bda07`): `src/lib/archive.ts` — which visits match a named place, which clusters are worth asking about, and what to say about each. Pure, 16 tests. Nothing is reachable from the UI yet; this is the arithmetic landing ahead of the build, the same split the geofence work used on 09-01.

**Task 3 — built and installed 2026-09-04, `b0ae3e3`.** `modules/timeline-import` walks the export with `android.util.JsonReader` in constant memory, so the 47 MB never crosses into JavaScript; `segments` comes back beside the visits because an empty list and a parser that threw look identical otherwise. **Runtime moved `5f318efe` to `5a67da27`** — the module directory, `expo-document-picker` and `expo-battery` are each a fingerprint input, so all three rode one APK.

Checked before the install rather than after: the APK carries the real hash and not the `file:fingerprint` placeholder, and its signer SHA-256 matches `android/app/debug.keystore`. `adb install -r` then kept everything — **157 sightings held, reaching back 13 days**, and this morning's six crossings still listed. The app launched clean, which is what says the lazy `requireNativeModule` held.

**The parser itself is still unexercised on the device.** Nothing calls it until Task 4 puts a screen in front of it, so *the module loaded* is not yet proved — only *the app did not crash without it*.

**Two bugs the tests caught while Gradle ran.** `archiveImport` opened its own `openSeenStore()` instead of going through `timeline.ts`, so it wrote to a different database than everything reads — an import that typechecks, reviews clean and lands nowhere. And `asSeen` dropped `import-enter`/`import-exit` on read: rows were written correctly and came back with no `via` at all, which would have counted 8,000 imported rows as app-open sightings.

**Not in this build, correcting earlier advice in this row.** Queue 18's real keystore is *not* free during a build that is happening anyway — a new key cannot update the installed app, so it costs the journal and the chat archive unless it is done as signing-scheme v3 rotation. The alarm intent needs its own design and tests. `expo-battery` is here for the fingerprint move only, so its feature JavaScript can now ship over the air without a second APK.

**Task 4 — built and published 2026-09-04 as `8e3de252`, runtime unmoved at `5a67da27`.** Settings → *Import your Timeline* picks the file with `copyToCacheDirectory: false`, so the 47 MB is read through the `content://` uri and never copied into the app. The preview names the file, the segment and visit counts, the date span, and a line per named place with **days as well as visits** — four visits across three days is three days of evidence, and a visit count reads as more history than there is. **Nothing is written until IMPORT.**

Places → Crossings recorded gains an IMPORTED line with FORGET beside it, kept apart from the measured count on purpose: 529 days of imported history and thirteen days of crossings are different claims, and one total would let the bigger stand for both. FORGET does not confirm — the argument for offering an import at all is that refusing it afterwards is free.

**The screen says which nothing it is.** Four different empty answers get four different sentences: a parser that threw (verbatim), a format Google changed (*"11,570 segments and no visits"*), a file whose visits are all outside any named circle, and a build without the native half. Those looked identical for as long as it took to ship one.

**Still unproved: the parser has never run.** Nothing had called it until this screen existed, and the device check has not happened yet — the phone locked itself before the import could be driven. *The module loads* and *the export parses* are both open questions, and the honest reading of this row is that the plumbing is complete and untested end to end.

**Task 5, the naming flow, is what remains.** The clusters are already computed and shown; what is missing is typing a name against one and re-running the match.

**Task 3 — the APK, and it cannot be split.** A streaming Kotlin parser in `modules/timeline-import`, because `JSON.parse` on 47 MB takes the phone down and `android.util.JsonReader` walks it in constant memory — the file never crosses into JavaScript. A new `modules/` directory moves the fingerprint and so does `expo-document-picker`, so both land in one local `./gradlew assembleRelease` signed with `android/app/debug.keystore`, or the phone is stranded.

**Tasks 4 and 5 — the screen and the naming.** Pick the file, see what it would add, agree to it, undo it in one gesture. Then the part that removes a real limit rather than adding a number: until now a place could only be named while standing in it with the app open, so he can now name somewhere he visited two hundred times last year. **By consent, never the Places API** — buying prettier labels by sending his place ids to Google is the one line every feature here has held.

**Two decisions the plan made that the spec had left open.** The spec said `via: 'import'`, one value: that cannot work, because an import writes a row for the arrival *and* one for the departure and telling those apart is the basis of every figure in `timeline.ts`. And **every existing truthiness check on `.via` silently meant *a geofence crossing*** — there were three, and left alone an import would have put 8,000 rows into the one diagnostic that made the geofence trustworthy, and would have let `alreadyInside` consult a visit Google recorded this morning and then refuse to announce a real arrival.

**What it unblocks, on the day it lands rather than in a fortnight.** Every habit figure rests on `ENOUGH_PLACE_DAYS = 4`; the export carries 344 days at the office and 516 at home. *"Usually you are there by 11:51 AM"* — a correct median over four app-opens by a man at his desk since ten — becomes **09:49 across 344 days**.
